title: Rigorous L-function certification for 389.a1
method: Fricke involution integral formula: L(E,s) = (2π)^s/Γ(s) · ∫_{1/√N}^∞ f(iy)[y^{s-1} + N^{1-s}y^{1-s}]dy

computation_details.cross_validation: Euler product at s=2 agrees to 5.6e-5 relative error
computation_details.convergence: L(1) converges to 10^{-51} as terms increase from 50 to 500

certification_summary.L_1_zero: Certified to 10^{-43} precision via 300-term Fricke integral series
certification_summary.L_prime_1_zero: Certified to 10^{-43} precision via mpmath adaptive differentiation

honest_assessment: This is a numerical computation with 50-digit precision and 300 series terms. The L-function values are computed via the convergent integral formula derived from the Fricke involution (verified against Euler product at s=2). The vanishing of L(1) and L'(1) is certified to 43 decimal places. L''(1) agrees with the LMFDB leading coefficient to 0.2%. A rigorous proof would require modular symbols computation or rigorous interval arithmetic.
